title: MoE Offloading Isn’t Always Faster: I Tested 5 Models on a 16GB GPU
why_read: A hands-on, data-driven exploration of MoE expert offloading strategies for running large language models on consumer GPUs with limited VRAM.
analysis: The author benchmarks five Mixture-of-Experts language models under different offloading strategies to see when selectively offloading just the MoE expert layers beats naive whole-layer offloading on a 16GB GPU. This is a genuinely useful, practical investigation for anyone trying to run large local models on consumer hardware, since offloading strategy can make a big difference in usable speed. The explanation of why MoE models offer this extra lever, because only a subset of experts activate per token, is clearly explained and technically sound. It's an informal benchmark rather than a rigorous paper, but the empirical results and reasoning are genuinely informative for local-LLM practitioners.
